title: BlueHarbor - Controls evidence & KMS integration sync
topics: KMS / HSM integration and key flow
summary: Redwood and BlueHarbor ran through BlueHarbor's SOC 2/ISO posture, focusing on getting timely access to Redwood's attestation reports via the portal, mapping controls to BlueHarbor's existing control matrix, and clarifying the KMS integration plan for Private deployments. Questions around audit log detail, log retention windows, and SAML identity provider flows were discussed. Agreed next steps include: provide scoped SOC 2 report link, share KMS integration diagram, schedule a technical runbook review with Devon and Marco, and a short pilot for log ingestion verification.
action_items: Aisha Patel: Send link to current SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary doc (due 2027-06-18)
Marco Diaz: Share KMS keyflow diagram and recommended envelope encryption pattern for Private deployments (due 2027-06-21)
Devon Reyes / Marco Diaz: Schedule 60-min runbook review for KMS onboarding and log access (due 2027-06-22)
Priya Nair: Provide customer control matrix template and highlight any non-standard evidence needs (due 2027-06-20)
next_steps: Redwood to habilitate trust portal account for BlueHarbor's GRC team and give read-only access to SOC2 artifacts
Run small pilot to verify audit log schema and retention (7-day window initially)
Follow-up call with infra deep-dive to review key rotation and HSM options
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Cara Li (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (BlueHarbor CISO), Omar Chen (Cloud Security Lead), Priya Nair (GRC Manager), Devon Reyes (Infra Engineer)

Auto-generated Summary:  Redlined - focus on SOC2 access, KMS key flow and evidence mapping.

Topics Covered: SOC2/ISO report access; evidence mapping; KMS/HSM integration; SSO/RBAC; audit log detail and residency; pilot plan for logs.

[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — we're on Pacific? or are most folks east?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: West coast for me, thanks. we wanted to make sure we cover the SOC 2 artifacts and how to get them into our control matrix, and then the KMS questions for private deployment.
[00:24] Aisha Patel: Perfect. I'll hand to Marco to do the technical outline and then we'll address access and evidence flow.
[00:34] Marco Diaz: Thanks. So high level, Redwood has two routes: hosted API where we provide attestation artifacts in the trust portal, and Private where you get a control plane but customer-managed networking and you can integrate your KMS. I want to focus on the KMS key flow we recommend and the audit logs you can expect.
[01:05] Omar Chen: Quick Q up front: BlueHarbor's requirement is that keys are customer-managed, or at least we must be able to rotate keys and have CNK — sorry, KMS rotation audit. Do you support HSM-backed customer keys?
[01:20] Marco Diaz: Yes, for Redwood Private we support customer KMS via standard envelope encryption patterns. We can integrate with most cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and with external HSMs via KMIP in some proven setups. There are a couple of caveats around key wrapping timing and cold key rotation that we should map in the runbook.
[01:45] Devon Reyes: When you say envelope encryption, are secrets written to Redwood storage encrypted with our CMK, or is there a separate wrapping key? I need to know what we can audit from our side.
[01:58] Marco Diaz: Good call out. The typical flow: ephemeral data keys are generated and wrapped with your CMK. The wrapped key is stored with the object - then at runtime Redwood unwraps with the CMK to decrypt. We'll share the diagram but the important part for audit is that key usage events (Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) appear in your KMS audit logs.
[02:18] Lena Ortiz: So we will see decrypt calls in AWS CloudTrail, yes?
[02:24] Marco Diaz: Correct. You should see KMS:Decrypt and GenerateDataKey calls in CloudTrail with the principal being the Redwood Private node role.
[02:35] Priya Nair: And for compliance evidence, what do you provide out of the trust portal vs what we need to request? For SOC2 we need the attestations plus underlying system descriptions.
[02:47] Aisha Patel: On our trust portal we publish the SOC 2 Type II report and a condensed controls mapping document — the typical deliverable for customers is: the attestation, a controls mapping (how Redwood maps to common SOC/ISO controls), the system security policy summary, and sample configurations. We don't dump raw logs into the portal; logs are available through integrations or during the runbook/pilot.
[03:12] Omar Chen: Are the control mappings machine-readable? our GRC tool prefers CSV/JSON exports to ingest evidence pointers.
[03:22] Aisha Patel: We can provide a spreadsheet CSV with control IDs, mapping, and typical evidence artifacts. We might need to tailor a few entries if you have non-standard control criteria.
[03:33] Priya Nair: Great. For the Type II period, can you confirm the coverage months? we need to confirm which date range the testing covered.
[03:42] Marco Diaz: Yes, we'll include the testing period in the report link. For the current Type II it'll show June 2026 - May 2027. I'll confirm exact dates in the email.
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: Okay — next, log retention. We have a requirement for 13 months retention in our archive for specific events. What's Redwood's retention default and options?
[04:08] Marco Diaz: Default hosted retention is 90 days of detailed logs and 13 months of aggregated audit events. For Private deployments you can configure long-term retention — either ship logs to your SIEM or plug object storage for archive (S3/GCS). The important piece is we can forward detailed token-level traces to your logging ingestion point.
[04:33] Devon Reyes: Does forwarding include the token text? PII concerns. We need redaction options.
[04:40] Marco Diaz: Good catch. We support redaction and partial token masking at the runtime layer. By default we do not forward plaintext user prompt tokens to external log sinks unless configured. There are explicit flags to enable full-text logging for troubleshooting; those should be enabled under controlled conditions with appropriate approvals.
[04:58] Lena Ortiz: Who on your side signs off on enabling full-text for our pilot?
[05:05] Cara Li: That would be CSM + SE approval — and we require a change ticket capturing the business justification. We'll put that into the runbook.
[05:14] [06:20]
[06:20] Omar Chen: Back to SSO — we run a SAML IdP. We need RBAC mappings from our groups to Redwood roles. Does Redwood support SCIM provisioning?
[06:32] Aisha Patel: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC roles can be mapped to groups from your IdP; you can define roles like read-only GRC, infra-admin, and audit-only. We have default role templates and you can request custom roles.
[06:50] Priya Nair: For audit purposes, do you capture admin activity in the trust portal? We need proof of who downloaded reports and who changed RBAC.
[06:58] Marco Diaz: Portal actions are logged; we capt- — sorry, the portal logs include user actions like report download, role changes, and API key rotations. Those logs can be exported and we can create an evidence snapshot for your audit window. Portal admin activity is also part of our SOC 2 scope.
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: On the control mapping we sent you a sample that expects evidence types like 'config snapshot', 'access list', 'change log'. I want to verify which artifacts you can produce natively versus which we will need to get during a live collection.
[07:31] Aisha Patel: Natively we can produce config snapshots for Redwood-managed control points, attestations, and portal admin logs. For customer-managed networking or customer KMS-specific artifacts (e.g., CloudTrail entries from your account), we can provide guidance and pointer to where you collect them, but the authoritative artifact will be in your account.
[07:53] Devon Reyes: So we'll be responsible for pulling KMS CloudTrail entries from our account showing key usage, and Redwood will provide mapping that shows where those logs correspond to the controls.
[08:03] Marco Diaz: Exactly. We'll mark those evidence pointers in the CSV so the evidence trail is clear.
[08:12] [09:10]
[09:10] Priya Nair: About encryption in transit, we need TLS details and cipher suites used, plus any mTLS options for Private.
[09:20] Marco Diaz: TLS 1.2/1.3 supported, we rotate certs centrally. For Private we support mTLS between your network boundary and the Redwood nodes; you can provide client certs for node authentication. We'll include an architecture snippet in the runbook with cipher list.
[09:40] Lena Ortiz: Is there a paper trail for certificate rotations? we need to show certificate lifecycle.
[09:47] Marco Diaz: Certificate events are logged in the portal audit logs and in our internal change logs; we can produce a certificate rotation timeline as part of the evidence pack.
[09:56] [12:05]
[12:05] Omar Chen: On the subject of on-call and incident response — for an incident involving key compromise, what's the sequence? who takes responsibility for revoking keys and rotating?
[12:18] Marco Diaz: If it's a hosted incident where Redwood KMS is used, Redwood executes the key rotation per our IR playbook and notifies customers. For customer-managed KMS, the customer performs key revocation in their KMS; Redwood will update the runbook steps to coordinate and will provide guidance for re-encrypting any at-rest data with the new key. We recommend pre-defining the trigger and communication channel in the SLA.
[12:42] Priya Nair: We need to ensure the IR playbook maps to our control for 'timely key rotation'. We'll send our table with response SLAs and Marco, you'll map Redwood's actions to each control?
[12:53] Marco Diaz: Yes, we can produce a mapping of our IR steps to control IDs as part of the artifact handoff.
[13:03] [15:30]
[15:30] Lena Ortiz: Aisha, can you confirm your SOC 2 auditor? Some of our auditors ask about the independence and testing firm.
[15:40] Aisha Patel: Our auditor is Brightwater Assurance — I'll include the auditor letter and scope in the portal link.
[15:49] Priya Nair: Great. For ISO27001, do you publish a certificate or a summary of scope?
[15:56] Aisha Patel: We have an ISO27001 certificate for platform operations — we publish the certificate and the scope summary in the portal. Full certificate copies are available on request.
[16:08] Omar Chen: When BlueHarbor required data residency earlier, we operate in EU and US regions. Can Redwood guarantee region-specific storage for logs and models?
[16:18] Marco Diaz: We have regioned deployments. For Private you can pin nodes to a region and we ensure data in transit and at rest remain in that region. For hosted tenants, we can confine training-free inference outputs and logs to a region depending on plan — we'll need to confirm the plan's residency guarantees and update the contract on that.
[16:40] Devon Reyes: Are backups stored cross-region? That could be a residency problem.
[16:46] Marco Diaz: By default backups for hosted are region-local but cross-region replication can be enabled — for regulated customers we disable cross-region backups unless requested. We'll call that out explicitly.
[16:58] [19:00]
[19:00] Priya Nair: For evidence handoff, do you support time-stamped snapshots? Auditors like immutable stamps.
[19:10] Cara Li: We can provide time-stamped artifact exports and hash digests for integrity verification. If you need S3-stored snapshots with object lock, we can coordinate a delivery model to your bucket.
[19:26] Lena Ortiz: Good. That's helpful. Omar — any infra follow-ups?
[19:31] Omar Chen: Yes — we want to test a short pilot to validate log schema. We'll set up a 7-day ingestion to our SIEM; during that period we want a test workload so we can see KMS decrypt events, a sample key rotation, and a portal download event.
[19:47] Marco Diaz: That aligns with our standard pilot. We'll generate a synthetic workload, enable the optional debug logs for a short window, and provide a checklist of config changes. Remember we need explicit approval for debug logs.
[20:05] [22:40]
[22:40] Devon Reyes: How does API key rotation work? we prefer ephemeral tokens with short TTLs and audit.
[22:49] Marco Diaz: We support short-lived tokens (OIDC flows) and long-live API keys; for production we recommend OIDC-based tokens with rotation. API key issuance and revocation are logged and visible in the portal.
[22:59] Priya Nair: Will revoked tokens show in an audit export?
[23:05] Marco Diaz: Yes, revocation events are captured.
[23:11] [27:15]
[27:15] Lena Ortiz: On the controls mapping deliverable, we want two things: a pre-populated mapping that aligns Redwood controls to our internal control IDs, and a playbook for evidence collection steps per control. Can you produce both?
[27:29] Aisha Patel: Yes — we normally provide a baseline mapping and then a tailor session where we adjust entries with the customer's GRC team. The playbook is the runbook we mentioned — it includes what artifacts to pull and who owns each item.
[27:43] Priya Nair: Please highlight any gaps — for example, network segmentation evidence that we may have to produce from our side.
[27:50] Marco Diaz: We'll flag gaps explicitly.
[27:56] [30:00]
[30:00] Omar Chen: A couple of edge cases: If we require HSM in our on-prem KMS, do you have experience integrating with Thales and Azure Dedicated HSM?
[30:12] Marco Diaz: We have prior integrations with Thales nShield and Azure Dedicated HSM through KMIP or cloud KMS connectors. Some adaptations are necessary per vendor but we've executed on similar customers. We'll share a vendor-specific checklist.
[30:27] Devon Reyes: For our CI/CD, we want to automate proof collection where possible — do you offer an API to pull evidence artifacts?
[30:38] Cara Li: There's an evidence API in the roadmap; currently we can automate exports via scheduled portal exports and S3 delivery. We'll include a manual-to-automated migration plan in the runbook.
[30:50] [33:07]
[33:07] Lena Ortiz: Aisha, will you send the portal invite to Priya and Omar? Priya needs read-only for the GRC ingestion and Omar needs admin for infra tasks.
[33:18] Aisha Patel: I'll provision two accounts: Priya as read-only GRC and Omar as infra-admin. We'll use SCIM to provision if you want.
[33:26] Priya Nair: SCIM would be ideal, yes.
[33:30] Aisha Patel: Noted.
[33:33] [36:45]
[36:45] Marco Diaz: One more technical note — audit logs granularity. For hosted customers we capture request metadata, routing decisions, model variant used, token counts, and error traces. We do not by default capture complete user prompt content unless debug is enabled. For Private we give you configuration knobs to adjust granularity before any logs leave your VPC.
[37:08] Devon Reyes: Will the metadata include client IP and node ID so we can map calls back to sessions?
[37:15] Marco Diaz: Yes, metadata includes client IP, session ID, node ID, model version, and relevant latency metrics.
[37:26] Priya Nair: That's useful. We'll map those fields to our evidence schema.
[37:32] [40:00]
[40:00] Lena Ortiz: I have one more ask on retention: if we need 36 months for certain audit artifacts, can you supply archived snapshots to our S3 with object lock and immutability?
[40:13] Marco Diaz: We can deliver snapshots to your S3 with object lock if required. That would be part of a contractual addendum for long-term archival. For the pilot we can do 13 months via your object storage.
[40:28] Omar Chen: Cost implications? we need a rough estimate for extended archival.
[40:33] Aisha Patel: We'll send a pricing appendix for long-term storage and transfer costs.
[40:38] [43:50]
[43:50] Priya Nair: For auditor interviews — will Redwood provide an SOC 2 point-of-contact for the auditor to validate evidence?
[43:58] Aisha Patel: Yes, we have a designated assurance contact who can coordinate evidence requests. We will provide their contact and SLA for evidence delivery.
[44:08] Lena Ortiz: Good.
[44:11] Devon Reyes: One more tiny bit: Our infra folks prefer logged events to include a trace id. Do you have correlation IDs across services?
[44:18] Marco Diaz: Yes, we propagate a correlation id across requests and logs. We'll include the schema.
[44:26] [47:00]
[47:00] Aisha Patel: Okay let's recap actions and due dates. Marco will share KMS keyflow diagram and vendor checklist by Monday the 21st. I will provision portal access and send the SOC 2 link by Friday the 18th. Priya you'll share the control matrix and mark any special evidence needs by the 20th. Devon and Marco will schedule the technical runbook session by the 22nd.
[47:26] Lena Ortiz: That sounds right. Any blockers?
[47:31] Omar Chen: None from our side. We just need to ensure the pilot has limited debug windows.
[47:36] Cara Li: We'll handle the approvals.
[47:40] [50:00]
[50:00] Priya Nair: Thanks all, this was helpful. One request: can you note in the mapping which controls require evidence from our tenant versus Redwood's? That will speed the auditor.
[50:11] Aisha Patel: Absolutely — we'll flag owner per-control in the CSV.
[50:18] Lena Ortiz: Great. We'll look for the next steps.
[50:23] Aisha Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the portal link, KMS diagram, and runbook invite.
[50:33] Meeting end: 16:55 UTC

Notes: occasional transcription errors expected (product names like 'KV cache' may be transcribed as 'kay vee cache'). References to internal docs: trust portal (https://redwood.example.com/trust) — placeholder link, KMS diagram (to be shared), pilot checklist (attached after call).
